newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close firmer in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close firmer in thin trading.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended firmer after a back-and-forth session on Monday, which saw the market take much of its direction from U.S. treasuries on light trading volumes.

"We are more or less following the U.S. Volume is really light. We have seen some buying in the morning but most accounts seem to be sitting on the sideline, not making any hasty decisions," said David Yu, a fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.26 to C$118.74 to yield 6.559 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.63 percent. The negative spread between the bonds was seven basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.

Canadian bonds initially opened higher with U.S. treasuries before markets in both countries turned lower in late morning trade. Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets recovered after U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips hinted there was no immediate need for a U.S. rate hike.
In Canada, dealers said volumes were light, with many traders awaiting economic data out later in the week.
Key releases out this week include the U.S. retail sales report for July out on Wednesday and the consumer price index for July on Thursday.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.19 to C$108.91 to yield 6.021 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.35 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 33 basis points from 31 basis points at Friday's close.
